decision: Reject implementing the strict two-pass normalization-certified replay: only 2318631 of 164967882 original OUT candidates (1.4055%) are certified removable, before any additional pass overhead. Residual-only interval equality holds for 100221835 candidates (60.7523%) under the original empirical projection envelope, but does not preserve the unrounded variance used by RMSNorm. Treat that broader selector solely as an unqualified follow-up hypothesis requiring actual replay and all512 raw GB10 tokens, first-logit tolerance and callbacks. Keep the read-only audit default-off; no measured candidate speedup or release qualification.
scope: Two new processes load the real model and run the original q8192/out512 prompt. Both use the same new whole-provider DLL and otherwise retain all268 verified archived runtime assets and original CLI. Both enable required-marker filtering; the read-only OUT consumer audit is the only environment difference. Each run carries all512 raw output IDs and actual callback IDs and the prompt-bound first-logit tolerance0.125. All original corrections still execute. The observer regenerates the original algorithm0 matrix in private storage, transports the existing PPB/Cauchy/midpoint envelope through BF16 residuals and the actual FMA variance reduction, then enumerates every FP32 variance up to4096 ULPs through the actual rsqrt function. Completed original outputs stand in for a hypothetical first replay pass where the residual interval is ambiguous. That candidate pass and any saved work are NOT executed or timed. Counts are classification diagnostics conditional on the existing empirical producer envelope, with all observed containment and endpoint differences reported separately. The model consumes only its original control. No candidate performance, prefix, long-context, package-soak or release qualification follows.
